title: Mysuru Dasara Ends With 417th Jamboo Savari Led by Elephant Prashanth
excerpt: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar flagged off the Vijayadashami finale at Mysore Palace, as Prashanth carried the 750-kg golden howdah to Bannimantap for the first time as lead elephant.
body:
• The 417th Jamboo Savari brought Mysuru Dasara to its grand finale on Wednesday, 21 October, with elephant Prashanth carrying the 750-kg golden howdah for the first time as lead elephant.
  • Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar flagged off the procession at Mysore Palace during the Shubha Meena Lagna, offering floral tributes to the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari.
  • The roughly 5-km procession ran from Mysore Palace to Bannimantap, where the evening closed with the torchlight parade, the Panjina Kavayathu, at 7 p.m.
  • Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan attended the finale alongside Shivakumar.

Mysuru Dasara reached its grand finale on Wednesday evening as the 417th Jamboo Savari set out from Mysore Palace, with the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari carried through the city in the golden howdah. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar flagged off the procession by offering floral tributes to the idol at the palace during the auspicious Shubha Meena Lagna, according to Nation Press. The floral tribute, the pushparchane, fell in the 4:10 p.m. to 4:35 p.m. muhurta set by the palace almanac.

The howdah elephant this year was Captain Prashanth, flanked by the kumki elephants Roopa and Cauvery. Prashanth has taken part in the Jamboo Savari 16 times, but 2026 was the first time he led the procession as the primary howdah-bearing elephant, carrying the roughly 750-kg golden howdah, known in Kannada as the Chinnada Ambari.

A 5-kilometre procession to Bannimantap

From the palace, the procession wound about 5 km through the old city to Bannimantap in the north of Mysuru, led by the howdah elephant and followed by decorated elephants, folk troupes, tableaux and police bands. The day had begun at the palace with the Nandi Dhwaja puja in the 1:36 p.m. to 1:56 p.m. window, according to the official schedule reproduced by Karnataka.com. Watching from the roadside was free, while seated enclosures cost between Rs. 1,500 and Rs. 6,500 per person.

"Shivakumar flagged off the procession by offering floral tributes to the idol at the palace during the auspicious Shubha Meena Lagna, according to Nation Press ."

Once the procession reached Bannimantap, the festival closed with the torchlight parade, the Panjina Kavayathu, at 7 p.m. — a display by military and police contingents that has ended Dasara day in Mysuru for generations.

Three chief ministers at the palace

Shivakumar was joined at the celebrations by Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, along with state ministers and officials. Shivakumar was accorded a guard of honour at Mysuru Airport on arrival and extended wishes to visitors, praying for the blessings of Goddess Chamundeshwari. He pointed to the festival's wider programme — an Indian Air Force air show, a drone display and the traditional Kambala buffalo race — as events that drew a strong public response this year.

The finale also strained the city's capacity. A large influx of domestic and international tourists for the Jamboo Savari left hotels and rooms in Mysuru, neighbouring Madikeri district and areas on the route to Bengaluru fully occupied, and Shivakumar acknowledged the inconvenience to visitors while noting the traffic management arrangements put in place.

From the Maharaja's ride to the goddess's

Mysuru Dasara, the Nada Habba or state festival of Karnataka, traces its celebrations to 1610 under Raja Wodeyar I, and under the Wadiyar kings the Maharaja himself rode in the golden howdah through the city. After Independence the festival passed to the state government, and the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari now rides in the howdah in place of the king. The howdah seat itself has passed between celebrated elephants: Arjuna carried it from 2012 to 2019 and Abhimanyu from 2020 to 2025, before Abhimanyu retired from howdah duty — a succession Prashanth now joins.

For the diaspora, the Jamboo Savari remains the defining image of Dasara: a royal procession preserved as a public state festival, unchanged in its essentials — the palace start, the golden howdah, the 5-km route and the torchlit close at Bannimantap — even as the cast of elephants and chief guests changes around it.
